report.summary: Outbox publication stalled to ~5-6 per 10 s against 28 arrivals, then caught up in a burst. The slow part of delivery is the consumer handler (~1.6 s on some attempts). The stall's mechanism is not confirmed.

findings.claim: Publications fell to about 5-6 per 10 s bucket while arrivals stayed at 28, then rose to 68-80 per bucket. Pending peaked at 134 and drained.
findings.reason: The per-bucket counts show a backlog that built, then drained, which matches late notifications.

findings.claim: Slow delivery time is in the consumer handler (p95 ~1605 ms, p50 0.024 ms). LedgerCore auth and unattributed time are small.
findings.reason: Total p95 of 1677 ms is almost entirely consumer handler time, with every attempt succeeding.

findings.claim: The ledgercore-local side looks healthy: transfers return 201 with p99 0.25 s, the pool has no waits or timeouts, and no DB blocking was sampled. A slow consumer handler is the likely cause of the throttled publishing.
findings.reason: The producer-side sources show no fault. All delivery attempts succeeded with no errors or retries, so the slowness sits in the consumer handler.

limitations: Only the earliest 100 of 421 delivery log rows are listed, so the timing of slow attempts within the window is not visible.
No poller-side or consumer-side timeline shows why publication dropped to about 5-6 per 10 s.
